To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a reduction in relative costs of information exchange leads to a denser social network, and a higher aggregate welfare.
a decrease in costs of linking leads to a more dispersed investment pattern and denser social network, but does not affect the access of individuals to information and welfare.
a decline in the costs of forming links in a network makes private investments more diffuse and gives rise to more links, and thus denser networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
information acquisition and exchange in social networks.
the role of social networks and social interactions in economic decision-making.
how information sharing in social networks is affected by the costs of linking and the costs of acquiring information privately.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Internet and the relative decline of the costs of private information and social networking have led to a significant increase in aggregate welfare.
the Internet and related computing technology have had a positive impact on social welfare, and that the impact is due to the increased ability of individuals to network.
the results of this experiment are consistent with the predictions of the model, and that the model is consistent with the results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Internet and social media are not only a source of information but a tool for information exchange and networking.
the Internet has made it easier for people to form links with one another and share information, and this has led to an overall increase in individual and social welfare.
social networks are not just a byproduct of information sharing, they are also a means for it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social network formation is an important determinant of the distribution of private investment, which in turn affects the aggregate level of information acquisition and welfare in a social network.
social network formation can be an important mechanism for the diffusion of information.
social networks can be a powerful tool for information sharing and that they can be improved through policy interventions that lower costs of linking.
